items.title: Family of 6 Builds Their Own House Out of Straw Bales | Start to Finish by @buildingroots5873
items.description: Most people would never expect to find straw inside a house wall. On their family farm in North Dakota, Wiley and Theressa built their entire home out of it. Nearly 300 feet of straw bale walls, some reaching 20 feet high. An earthen floor made from sand, soil and chopped straw. Sheep's wool insulation. A living room ceiling finished with fire. A railing built from old rebar and leftover redwood. And four kids who didn't watch it happen — they helped. Building Roots - Alternative living https://www.youtube.com/@buildingroots5873

items.title: Family of 10 Turns a School Bus Into a Home With 7 Beds | Start to Finish by @TheBusLifeShow
items.description: Seven kids, two parents, and one completely empty school bus. Thirty-eight feet of bare metal that somehow has to become a home they can live in full-time. Shane and Julie raised the roof, cut in eight new windows, and built seven beds into a space most people would struggle to fit a family of four. There's a kitchen, a bathroom, a dinette that changes jobs every few hours — and yes, a wood stove. The kids helped build it. And before the bus was finished, the family got one bigger. items.title: Man Builds a Solar Powered Boat from Old Steel Barrels | Start to Finish by @TNCreativeProject​
items.description: Most people look at a pile of rusted steel barrels and see scrap. He looked at the same pile and saw a boat. No fuel. No exhaust. No engine noise. Just sunlight, a homemade steel frame, and a handful of barrels that were headed for the scrapyard. Even the steering came from somewhere unexpected. Months of cutting and welding, all leading to one question: will it float? items.title: Man Spends Years Rebuilding an Abandoned Stone House in the Forest Alone | by @luxonbushcraft​
items.description: Twenty years ago, Martin decided he wanted a different kind of life — quieter, simpler, closer to nature. Years later he found an abandoned stone house, built in 1957 and forgotten in the forest for decades. Most people would have walked away. This is the full story of what happened next: a new roof, stone walls repaired one by one, insulation, a handmade front door, a wood stove, solar panels, a covered terrace built from massive natural timber, an outdoor kitchen, and a garden — almost all of it built alone, with his dog Laika beside him. In this video Martin also tells the story himself: why he chose a ruin, when he almost gave up, and what viewers never see behind the finished footage. Luxon Bushcraft https://www.youtube.com/@luxonbushcraft https://www.facebook.com/luxonbuschcraft https://www.instagram.com/luxonbushcraft/ 00:00 An Abandoned Stone House from 1957 02:05 A New Metal Roof Goes On 04:50 What Was Hiding Behind the Old Plaster 07:22 Waterproofing and the New Concrete Floor 09:32 Windows In, Old Floor Out 12:10 Insulating the Roof 14:35 Timber Cladding Transforms the Interior 17:00 Wood Stove, Solar Power and a Handmade Door 21:10 Building the Staircase 23:25 Furniture Made for This House Only 26:40 Stone Steps and the Entrance 30:45 The Covered Terrace Begins 39:32 The Outdoor Kitchen 45:39 Finishing the Terrace Roof 50:00 Why He Never Gave Up

Every piece of furniture is built by hand to fit the space exactly.

items.title: Man Builds a Massive Glass A-Frame on a Remote Mountain | Start to Finish by @LankHome
items.description: What does it take to build a luxury A-Frame mountain house with a dream pool — from an empty hillside to a fully finished home? In this full build documentary, a civil engineer with real-world construction experience takes on one of the most ambitious residential projects imaginable. Built on challenging mountainous terrain, this A-Frame house features panoramic mountain views, floor-to-ceiling glazing, a traditional brick fireplace, radiant floor heating, a designer circular swimming pool, and a breathtaking glass-enclosed living space that brings the outdoors in. Every phase of construction is captured — from the reinforced concrete foundation and massive timber A-frame structure, to the pool tiling, interior finishing, landscaping, and final furnishing. items.title: Man Builds $20,000 Buggy With Motorcycle Engine | Start to Finish by @homemade_madness
items.description: Meet Jornt, a young builder from the Netherlands who set out to create a high-performance off-road buggy almost entirely from scratch. Using a Honda CBR 1000 engine, recycled car parts, and countless hours of problem-solving, he transformed a simple idea into the Homemade Madness Cheetah Buggy. From designing the chassis and suspension to fabricating the drivetrain, steering, and exhaust system, every step was built in his home workshop. The result is a lightweight, fast machine that proves creativity and determination can rival even the most expensive factory-built vehicles. Watch the complete build from start to finish. Deep in the mountains, Nik — alongside friends and family — slowly raised a massive handcrafted home log by log, season after season. This is not a polished TV project or a fast construction build. It’s years of real craftsmanship, setbacks, problem-solving, exhaustion, and persistence captured step by step. Every beam, every wall, and every detail carries the effort of countless days spent working in the wilderness.
